headline: Approved Stack Storage changes at 679 Main Street, Library Commons updates, and plan to sell city parcels.
summary: The board adopted the Comprehensive Plan update and agreed to clarify that orientation limits apply only to signs over 80 square feet. It also asked the City Councilor for more information on two marijuana facility applications. Hearings on a parking reduction at 61-69 Suffolk Street and a fence height permit at 230-232 Beech Street were continued to October 13, 2026.
decisions: Continued the parking reduction special permit hearing for 61-69 Suffolk Street because the applicant was not present.
Continued the fence height permit hearing for 230-232 Beech Street because the applicant was not present and a board member was attending a site visit.
Continued the Comprehensive Plan revisions zone change hearing after an update from Lauren Niles.
Approved plan to combine parcels 3 and 4 for sale to the Log Cabin and sell parcels 1 and 2 (54 acres) for conservation, 4-0.
Approved three notices of decision for Library Commons Phase 2 project updates, 4-0.
Approved amendments to the Stack Storage project at 679 Main Street, 4-0.
Approved sending a letter to City Councilor asking for more information on the 'Diablo Man' LLC marijuana application at 73 Sargeant Street, 4-0.
Approved sending a letter to City Councilor asking for more information on the Red Barn Growers' LLC marijuana application at 1 Cabot Street, 4-0.
Approved minutes of earlier meetings, except 3/28/23, 11/12/24, 5/14/24, and 8/25/26, which were continued to October 13, 2026, 4-0.
Continued the parking reduction special permit hearing for 61-69 Suffolk Street to October 13, 2026, 5-0.
Continued the fence height permit hearing for 230-232 Beech Street to October 13, 2026, 5-0.
Agreed to clarify that the BG sign orientation restrictions apply only to signs over 80 square feet.
Adopted the Comprehensive Plan update after reviewing revised materials from staff.
Continued the Comprehensive Plan revisions hearing to October 27, 2026, 5-0.

5. **ANR** City of Holyoke / Conservation, (212-00-001) Joseph Pellegrini presented a proposal to combine parcels 3 and 4 and sell them to the Log Cabin, while parcels 1 and 2 (54 acres) would be declared surplus and sold to the Massachusetts Department of Fish and Game for conservation. - Paul Burns-Johnson, Member ... Yes

1.) **Project Updates / Old Business / New Business:**
- a.) Comprehensive Plan Update/Discussion
- b.) SPR Amendment #3, n/f Library Commons Phase 2:
  - 1. Bldg B, 344 Appleton Street
  - 2. Bldg C, 188-190 Chestnut Street
  - 3. Bldg D, 207 Elm Street

Liam Brenier presented changes to the demolition plans for multiple sites, including the relocation of transformers, propane tanks, and trees due to clearance and infrastructure constraints. Some changes, such as transformer and termination cabinet installation, have been completed, while others like sidewalks and dumpster enclosures remain pending. The team discussed material changes from asphalt to concrete sidewalks and adjustments to fence lines and propane tank locations to meet requirements and improve accessibility. The board reviewed and approved draft decisions for three notices of decision related to project updates, including changes to Site 3 Building D where the contractor replaced the asphalt alleyway with concrete and made grading improvements without requiring grade walls. Jeff confirmed he had forwarded the plans to the city engineer without receiving any issues, and the board voted to approve the notices of decision. The motion was made by Kate Kruckemeyer and seconded by Paul Burns-Johnson. The motion carried 4-0 by roll call vote as follows:
- Rosanna Lopez, Member ... Yes
- Paul Burns-Johnson, Member ... Yes
- Kate Kruckemeyer, Vice-Chairperson ... Yes
- Scott Geiger, Member ...

- c.) SPR Amendment #1, 'Stack Storage' 679 Main Street; NOD item #14 Robert Levesque presented updates and shared his screen to show the revised plans. The board reviewed and approved amendments to the Stack Storage project at 679 Main Street, with changes focused on traffic flow modifications and curb cuts as requested by MassDOT. The motion was made by Kate Kruckemeyer and seconded by Paul Burns-Johnson. The motion carried 4-0 by roll call vote as follows:
- Rosanna Lopez, Member ... Yes
- Paul Burns-Johnson, Member ... Yes
- Kate Kruckemeyer, Vice-Chairperson ... Yes
- Scott Geiger, Member ... Yes

- d.) Section 7.10 Marijuana Facilities, marijuana review, 'Diablo Man' LLC, 73 Sargeant Street (MME) The Board reviewed the applications but found them incomplete and approved letters be sent to City Councilor requesting more information.
- e.) Section 7.10 Marijuana Facilities, marijuana review, Red Barn Growers' LLC, 1 Cabot Street, 2B (MME) The Board reviewed the applications but found them incomplete and approved letters be sent to City Councilor requesting more information.

The motion was made by Kate Kruckemeyer and seconded by Paul Burns-Johnson. The motion carried 4-0 by roll call vote as follows:
